story.head: Trench warfare
paras: The Senators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-1 in Ottawa on Oct 21. The Panthers (13-8-3) beat Buffalo 4-3 on Saturday, and the Sens have won two in a row. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Senators first (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Panthers fifth (tied for 11th).
The Senators’ record (.700) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.616), largely because they’re 8-3 in one-goal games. The Panthers’ record (.604) is about what their chances are worth.

The Panthers (1st) and the Senators (2nd) both hound the puck on the forecheck. The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (2nd). As for the Panthers, they don’t block many shots (32nd). Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one. On top of that, both teams like to hit, especially the Panthers (1st), so expect plenty of it.

Tim Stützle (13 G / 18 A / 31 P in 25 GP) is carrying the Senators’ offense, with seven points in his last five games. Drake Batherson (12 G / 10 A / 22 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind, with a point in six straight games against Florida. Matthew Tkachuk (7 G / 25 A / 32 P in 24 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, and Sam Reinhart (12 G / 11 A / 23 P in 24 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Linus Ullmark (12-1-0 / .941 SV% in 13 GS) has been outstanding for Ottawa and is expected to start. Jacob Markström (7-4-1 / .893 SV% in 13 GS) is expected to go for Florida.

lean.FLA: Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Florida has home-ice advantage and gets Barkov back. The Panthers can tip it if their penalty kill holds up.
